newsitem.title: DUBAI: Bahrain to attend EU-GCC meeting in Doha.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain to attend EU-GCC meeting in Doha.

text.p: Bahrain, locked in a territorial dispute with Qatar, will attend a Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) ministerial meeting and a joint European Union meeting to be held in Doha on February 17, the official Gulf News Agency (GNA) reported on Saturday.

"Bahrain has decided to participate in this meeting based on directions by Bahrain's emir Sheikh Isa bin Sulman al-Khalifa and on its belief in common Gulf interests," said GNA quoting a foreign ministry official.
GNA said Bahrain's Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammad bin Mubarak al-Khalifa will head his country's delegation to the meetings.
Qatar and Bahrain have been locked for decades in a dispute over a cluster of islands, sanbanks and reefs in the Gulf controlled by Bahrain since the 1930s but also claimed by Qatar.
Ties between the two GCC states worsened after Bahrain accused two Qataris of spying and boycotted the council's December summit in Doha.
Bahrain pardoned the two Qataris later in December after a state security court sentenced them to three years in jail.
A mediation committee of foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Oman and Kuwait was set up by the GCC, an economic and political alliance to which Bahrain and Qatar also belong.
Bahraini Crown Prince Sheikh Hamad bin Isa al-Khalifa and Qatari Foreign Minister Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabr al-Thani, held talks in London on Friday in an attempt to ease strained relations.
